pick.headline: Mortar shell kills dozens in Sarajevo market
pick.summary: On February 5, 1994, a mortar shell struck the Markale open-air market in Sarajevo, killing 68 people.
pick.significance: The massacre prompted a NATO ultimatum for the withdrawal of Serb heavy weapons from around Sarajevo, the first step toward NATO military involvement in Bosnia.
pick.fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of February 7, 1994, carried Paris AFP on Lord Owen, after meeting Milosevic, saying "nobody but a fool" wanted air strikes in retaliation for the Saturday mortar attack on a Sarajevo market that killed 68 people, but nobody could go on tolerating it either.
